id_and_class.summary: Manel Pretel-Wilson argues that the concept of consciousness, inherited from Descartes’s split between a thinking subject and an extended world, should be replaced by spatial and temporal dualities that structure everything that exists. For human beings the key duality is between the actual and the possible, realized through human systems that people build together to shape the human world.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Pretel-Wilson identifies nothing as consciousness; he holds that the concept becomes redundant once the spatial duality (peripheral and central, inner and outer) and the temporal duality (actual and possible) of beings are made clear.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: He rejects the Cartesian split of mind and body. Inner and outer are two sides of one spatial duality, so organism and environment, and human beings and the human world, cannot be separated.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (consciousness is treated as a redundant concept, superseded by spatial and temporal dualities)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Human beings are defined by creating rather than thinking or perceiving: a ‘utopico-practical being’ that works with others to realize ideas and purposes in the world.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Spatial and temporal dualities constituting everything that exists, organisms functionally tied to their environments, and human systems that realize shared purposes.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through systems-theoretic and historical-philosophical analysis of the concepts of mind and consciousness.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A spatial duality of peripheral and central shared by all sentient beings, and a temporal duality of actual and possible specific to human systems.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Agency and purpose (human systems); phenomenal consciousness set aside as redundant
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The actual–possibility duality: human beings, working through shared systems, turn possible states into actual ones and so shape the human world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In the functional relation between beings and their worlds: organisms with environments, human beings with the human world built by human systems.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Human systems act as the architects of the human world, realizing human purposes; this replaces the explanatory job usually given to consciousness.
core_claims_and_evidence: The concept of consciousness comes from Descartes’s opposition between a thinking subject and an external world.
Inner and outer are two sides of one spatial duality, ruling out a split between organism and environment.
The actual–possibility duality of human systems explains human agency without a ‘collective person’ with its own consciousness or an ‘artificial man’ without its own purpose.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: If consciousness is redundant, the framework still has to say what anchors subjective experience.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent in rejecting mind–body dualism, but it replaces one dualism with others (spatial and temporal) whose status needs further specification.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Pretel-Wilson locates purpose in human beings working together through human systems to realize ideas that shape the human world.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Utopics: The Unification of Human Science, Manel Pretel-Wilson
The Ethics of Human Systems: Creating Economic Value with Impact for Good, Manel Pretel-Wilson
